page: Microsoft Azure GS1 is a memory-optimized server instance within the GS family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor running at 2.0 GHz. This configuration provides 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs, with 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. The instance is equipped with 28.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 14.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 57 GB volume, and there are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the GS1 instance delivers lower-tier computational performance. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (835.0) and multi-core (1587.88) CPU performance fall into the bottom 10% category. Similarly, the Passmark CPU score of 2083.88 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1942.0 are positioned in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 181.13 GB/sec (bottom 25%), which drops to 20.49 GB/sec for large uncached blocks (bottom 10%). However, single-threaded gzip compression achieves an average tier throughput of 23.85 GB/sec, representing a relative strength compared to its other processing metrics.

The primary tradeoff of the GS1 server is its high memory allocation relative to its limited processing power. While the 28.0 GB of RAM provides substantial capacity for memory-bound tasks, the underlying Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor limits throughput for compute-heavy operations, as evidenced by weak database operations (1067.28 on Passmark) and poor static web serving throughput (2.38 GB/sec). Qualitatively, the instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU density, but its low benchmark-per-resource efficiency makes it less suitable for CPU-intensive workloads. It is best aligned with lightweight memory-intensive workloads, basic caching, or small-scale database operations that require a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose instances but do not demand high CPU throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure GS1 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 28.0 GB of RAM, running on a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it includes 57 GB of local storage and no GPU. Benchmarks show poor to weak performance across most categories, with stress-ng CPU scores and large-block memory bandwidth falling into the bottom 10%. However, it maintains average single-threaded gzip compression at 23.85 GB/sec. The instance's high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 14.0 GB per core makes it suitable for memory-intensive but computationally light workloads, such as basic caching or small database tasks, though it presents a clear tradeoff in raw processing power.
